units.Ezekiel 17:1: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 17:2: “Son of man, tell a story and speak a parable to the house of Israel,
units.Ezekiel 17:3: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: The great eagle, with great wings and a broad span, full of talons, which has authority to enter Lebanon, took the cedar’s choice parts;
units.Ezekiel 17:4: he nipped off the tips of its tender growth, carried them to the land of Canaan, and set them in a fortified city.
units.Ezekiel 17:5: He took some of the land’s seed and put it in the plain, a plant beside abundant water; he appointed it to be watched over.
units.Ezekiel 17:6: It sprouted and became a weak vine, small in size so that it might appear. Its branches were upon it and its roots beneath it. It became a vine, produced offshoots and extended its climbing growth.
units.Ezekiel 17:7: There was another great eagle, with great wings and many talons. Behold, this vine was intertwined toward him, its roots toward him; it sent its branches to him to water it together with the clod of its planting.
units.Ezekiel 17:8: It grows fat in a good plain beside abundant water, to produce shoots, bear fruit and become a great vine.
units.Ezekiel 17:9: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Will it prosper? Will not the roots of its tender growth and its fruit rot, and all its early shoots dry up? No great arm or numerous people will be needed to pull it from its roots.
units.Ezekiel 17:10: Behold, it grows fat—surely it will not prosper? Will it not dry up completely as soon as the scorching wind touches it? It will dry up together with the clod of its growth.’”
units.Ezekiel 17:11: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 17:12: “Son of man, say now to the embittering house, ‘Do you not understand what these things were?’ Say, ‘When Babylon’s king comes against Jerusalem, he will take her king and her rulers and bring them to himself in Babylon.
units.Ezekiel 17:13: He will take one of the royal seed, make a covenant with him, and bring him under a curse-oath. He will take the land’s leaders,
units.Ezekiel 17:14: so that it may become a weak kingdom, not exalt itself at all, and keep his covenant and establish it.
units.Ezekiel 17:15: He will revolt from him, sending his messengers to Egypt to give him horses and many people. Will he prosper? Will the one doing contrary things be rescued? Will one transgressing a covenant be saved?
units.Ezekiel 17:16: As I live, says the Lord, surely in the place of the king who made him king—he who dishonored My curse-oath and transgressed My covenant—with him in the midst of Babylon he will die.
units.Ezekiel 17:17: Pharaoh will not wage war against him with great power or a numerous crowd, amid siegeworks and the building of missile stations to remove lives.
units.Ezekiel 17:18: He dishonored a sworn oath by transgressing a covenant; behold, he has given his hand and did all these things to him. Surely he will not be saved?
units.Ezekiel 17:19: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: As I live, surely My covenant that he transgressed and My sworn oath that he dishonored—I will bring them upon his head.
units.Ezekiel 17:20: I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in his enclosure.
units.Ezekiel 17:21: In all his battle array they will fall by the sword, and I will scatter the survivors to every wind. You will recognize that I, the Lord, have spoken.’
units.Ezekiel 17:22: For thus says the Lord: I Myself will take from the cedar’s choice parts, nip off from the top of their heart, and I Myself will plant it upon a high mountain. I will suspend it
units.Ezekiel 17:23: upon Israel’s lofty mountain and plant it. It will produce a shoot, bear fruit and become a great cedar. Every beast will rest beneath it, every bird will rest under its shade, and its branches will be restored.
units.Ezekiel 17:24: All the plain’s trees will know that I am the Lord who lowers a high tree, raises a low tree, dries a green tree and makes a dry tree flourish. I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.”
units.Ezekiel 18:1: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 18:2: “Son of man, what is this proverb you have among Israel’s sons, saying, ‘The fathers ate unripe grapes, and the children’s teeth were set on edge’?
units.Ezekiel 18:3: As I live, says the Lord, this proverb will certainly no longer be spoken in Israel.
units.Ezekiel 18:4: For all souls are Mine. As the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son—they are Mine. The soul that sins will die.
units.Ezekiel 18:5: The person who is righteous, practicing judgment and righteousness,
units.Ezekiel 18:6: will not eat upon the mountains, certainly will not raise his eyes to the reflections of the house of Israel, certainly will not defile his neighbor’s wife, and will not approach a woman in her menstrual separation;
units.Ezekiel 18:7: he certainly will not oppress anyone, will return a debtor’s pledge, takes no plunder, will give his bread to the hungry, and will clothe the naked;
units.Ezekiel 18:8: he will not give his silver at interest or take increase, will turn his hand from injustice, and will render a righteous judgment between a man and his neighbor;
units.Ezekiel 18:9: he has walked in My commands and kept My ordinances to carry them out. This one is righteous; he will surely live, says the Lord.
units.Ezekiel 18:10: But if he fathers a pestilent son who sheds blood and commits sins,
units.Ezekiel 18:11: he did not walk in the way of his righteous father, but even ate upon the mountains and defiled his neighbor’s wife,
units.Ezekiel 18:12: oppressed the poor and needy, seized plunder, did not return a pledge, set his eyes upon idols, and has committed lawlessness,
units.Ezekiel 18:13: gave at interest and took increase—this one certainly will not live. He committed all this lawlessness; he will surely be put to death, and his blood will be upon him.
units.Ezekiel 18:14: But if he fathers a son who sees all the sins his father committed, becomes afraid, and does not act according to them,
units.Ezekiel 18:15: he has not eaten upon the mountains, not set his eyes upon the reflections of the house of Israel, and not defiled his neighbor’s wife,
units.Ezekiel 18:16: has not oppressed anyone, not taken a pledge, and not seized plunder; he gave his bread to the hungry and clothed the naked,
units.Ezekiel 18:17: and turned his hand from injustice, did not take interest or increase, practiced righteousness and walked in My commands. He will not die in his father’s injustices; he will surely live.
units.Ezekiel 18:18: But if his father practiced affliction and seized plunder, he did contrary things in the midst of My people and will die in his injustice.
units.Ezekiel 18:19: You will say, ‘Why did the son not receive his father’s injustice?’ Because the son practiced righteousness and mercy, preserved all My ordinances and carried them out; he will surely live.
units.Ezekiel 18:20: The soul that sins will die. The son will not receive his father’s injustice, nor the father his son’s injustice. The righteous person’s righteousness will be upon him, and the lawless person’s lawlessness upon him.
units.Ezekiel 18:21: If the lawless person turns from all the lawlessness he committed, keeps all My commandments, and practices righteousness and mercy, he will surely live; he certainly will not die.
units.Ezekiel 18:22: None of the transgressions he committed will be remembered. By the righteousness he practiced, he will live.
units.Ezekiel 18:23: Do I at all desire the death of the lawless, says the Lord, rather than his turning from his evil way and living?
units.Ezekiel 18:24: But when a righteous person turns from his righteousness and practices injustice according to all the lawlessness the lawless person committed, none of the righteous acts he did will be remembered. In the transgression he committed and the sins he sinned, in these he will die.
units.Ezekiel 18:25: You said, ‘The Lord’s way does not run straight.’ Hear now, the whole house of Israel: Surely My way does not fail to run straight? Is it not your way that fails to run straight?
units.Ezekiel 18:26: When the righteous person turns from his righteousness, commits a transgression and dies, in the transgression he committed—in it he will die.
units.Ezekiel 18:27: When a lawless person turns from the lawlessness he practiced and practices judgment and righteousness, this one has preserved his life
units.Ezekiel 18:28: and turned from all the impieties he committed; he will surely live, he certainly will not die.
units.Ezekiel 18:29: The house of Israel says, ‘The Lord’s way does not go right.’ Surely My way does not fail to go right, house of Israel? Is it not your way that fails to go right?
units.Ezekiel 18:30: I will judge you, each according to his way, house of Israel, says the Lord. Turn back and turn away from all your impieties, and they will not become a punishment of injustice for you.
units.Ezekiel 18:31: Cast away from yourselves all your impieties with which you acted impiously against Me, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why are you dying, house of Israel?
units.Ezekiel 18:32: For I do not desire the death of the one who dies, says the Lord.”
units.Ezekiel 19:1: “And you, take up a lament over Israel’s ruler,
units.Ezekiel 19:2: and say: What was your mother? A cub! She came to be among lions; among lions she multiplied her cubs.
units.Ezekiel 19:3: One of her cubs sprang away; he became a lion, learned to seize prey, and ate human beings.
units.Ezekiel 19:4: Nations heard against him; he was caught in their destruction, and they led him with a muzzle to Egypt’s land.
units.Ezekiel 19:5: She saw that he had been driven away from her and that her support had perished; she took another of her cubs and appointed him a lion.
units.Ezekiel 19:6: He moved among lions, became a lion, learned to seize prey, and ate human beings.
units.Ezekiel 19:7: He fed in his boldness, desolated their cities, and destroyed the land and its fullness by the sound of his roaring.
units.Ezekiel 19:8: Nations from the surrounding countries set themselves against him and spread their nets over him; he was caught in their destruction.
units.Ezekiel 19:9: They put him in a muzzle and a cage. He came to Babylon’s king, and he brought him into prison, so that his voice would not be heard upon Israel’s mountains.
units.Ezekiel 19:10: Your mother was like a vine, like a blossom on a pomegranate tree, planted by water; her fruit and her shoot came from abundant water.
units.Ezekiel 19:11: She had a rod of strength for a tribe of leaders; it rose in her size among the trunks, and it saw her size among the multitude of her branches.
units.Ezekiel 19:12: She was broken off in wrath and thrown to the ground. The scorching wind dried her choice parts; her rod of strength was punished and dried up. Fire consumed her.
units.Ezekiel 19:13: Now they have planted her in the wilderness, in a waterless land,
units.Ezekiel 19:14: and fire went out from a rod of her choice parts and devoured her, and there was no rod of strength in her. A tribe is for a parable of lament, and it will become a lament.”
units.Ezekiel 20:1: In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, men from the elders of the house of Israel came to question the Lord and sat before me.
units.Ezekiel 20:2: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 20:3: “Son of man, speak to Israel’s elders and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Have you come to question Me? As I live, I will certainly not answer you, says the Lord.’
units.Ezekiel 20:4: Shall I indeed exact retribution upon them? Son of man, solemnly testify to them about their fathers’ lawlessness,
units.Ezekiel 20:5: and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: From the day I chose the house of Israel, I became known to the seed of Jacob’s house and was known to them in Egypt’s land. I supported them with My hand, saying, “I am the Lord your God.”
units.Ezekiel 20:6: On that day I supported them with My hand to bring them out of Egypt’s land into the land I prepared for them, a land flowing with milk and honey; it is a honeycomb compared with all the earth.
units.Ezekiel 20:7: I said to them, “Let each cast away the abominations of his eyes, and do not be defiled by Egypt’s practices. I am the Lord your God.”
units.Ezekiel 20:8: They revolted from Me and would not listen to Me. They did not cast away the abominations of their eyes or abandon Egypt’s practices. I said I would pour My wrath upon them and complete My anger in them in the midst of Egypt’s land.
units.Ezekiel 20:9: I acted so that My name would not be profaned at all before the nations among whom they are, among whom I was known to them before their eyes by bringing them out of Egypt’s land.
units.Ezekiel 20:10: I brought them out of Egypt’s land and brought them into the wilderness,
units.Ezekiel 20:11: and gave them My commands and made My ordinances known to them, which a person will carry out and by which he will live.
units.Ezekiel 20:12: I gave them My sabbaths as a sign between Me and them, so that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
units.Ezekiel 20:13: I said to the house of Israel in the wilderness, “Walk in My commands.” But they did not walk, and they rejected My ordinances, which a person will carry out and by which he will live; they greatly profaned My sabbaths. I said I would pour My wrath upon them in the wilderness to consume them utterly.
units.Ezekiel 20:14: I acted so that My name would not be profaned at all before the nations from whom I brought them out before their eyes.
units.Ezekiel 20:15: I too raised My hand against them in the wilderness, that I would not bring them at all into the land I gave them, a land flowing with milk and honey, a honeycomb compared with all the earth,
units.Ezekiel 20:16: because they rejected My ordinances, did not walk in My commands, and were profaning My sabbaths, and they followed the reflections of their hearts.
units.Ezekiel 20:17: My eye spared them from obliteration, and I did not make a complete end of them in the wilderness.
units.Ezekiel 20:18: I said to their children in the wilderness, “Do not walk in your fathers’ ordinances, do not keep their judgments, do not mix yourselves with their practices, and do not be defiled.
units.Ezekiel 20:19: I am the Lord your God. Walk in My commands, keep My ordinances and carry them out,
units.Ezekiel 20:20: and sanctify My sabbaths; let it be a sign between Me and you, so that you may know that I am the Lord your God.”
units.Ezekiel 20:21: Their children too embittered Me. They did not walk in My commands or keep My ordinances to carry them out, which a person will carry out and by which he will live; they were profaning My sabbaths. I said I would pour My wrath upon them in the wilderness and complete My anger upon them.
units.Ezekiel 20:22: I acted so that My name would not be profaned at all before the nations from whom I brought them out before their eyes.
units.Ezekiel 20:23: I raised My hand against them in the wilderness, to scatter them among the nations and disperse them among the countries,
units.Ezekiel 20:24: because they did not carry out My ordinances, rejected My commands and were profaning My sabbaths, while their eyes followed their fathers’ reflections.
units.Ezekiel 20:25: I too gave them commands that were not good, and ordinances in which they would not live.
units.Ezekiel 20:26: I will defile them through their gifts, when I pass through every one who opens the womb, so that I may destroy them.
units.Ezekiel 20:27: Therefore speak to the house of Israel, son of man, and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: To this extent your fathers angered Me in the transgressions they committed against Me.
units.Ezekiel 20:28: I brought them into the land I raised My hand to give them. They saw every high hill and every shady tree; there they sacrificed to their gods, there they set a fragrant aroma, and there they poured their libations.
units.Ezekiel 20:29: I said to them, “What is Abama, that you go in there?” They called its name Abama to this very day.’
units.Ezekiel 20:30: Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord: Are you being defiled in your fathers’ lawlessness and prostituting yourselves after their abominations?
units.Ezekiel 20:31: In the firstfruits of your gifts, in your separations, you are being defiled with all your reflections to this very day. Shall I answer you, house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord, I will certainly not answer you, nor will this rise upon your spirit.
units.Ezekiel 20:32: It will not be as you say: “We will be like the nations and like the tribes of the earth, serving woods and stones.”
units.Ezekiel 20:33: Therefore, as I live, says the Lord, with a mighty hand, a high arm and outpoured wrath I will reign over you.
units.Ezekiel 20:34: I will bring you out from the peoples and receive you from the countries where you were scattered, with a mighty hand, a high arm and outpoured wrath.
units.Ezekiel 20:35: I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples and contend with you there, face to face.
units.Ezekiel 20:36: As I contended with your fathers in the wilderness of Egypt’s land, so I will judge you, says the Lord.
units.Ezekiel 20:37: I will lead you beneath My rod and bring you in by number,
units.Ezekiel 20:38: and select from you the impious and those who have revolted, for I will bring them out of their sojourning, but they will not enter Israel’s land. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
units.Ezekiel 20:39: And you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Each of you, remove his practices! After these things, if you are not listening to Me, you will no longer profane My holy name with your gifts and practices.
units.Ezekiel 20:40: For upon My holy mountain, upon a high mountain, says the Lord, the Lord, there the whole house of Israel will serve Me to the end. There I will accept, and there I will attend to your firstfruits and the firstfruits of your separations, with all your holy things.
units.Ezekiel 20:41: As a fragrant aroma I will accept you when I bring you out from the peoples and receive you from the countries where you were scattered. I will be sanctified among you before the eyes of the peoples.
units.Ezekiel 20:42: You will recognize that I am the Lord when I bring you into Israel’s land, into the land for which I raised My hand to give it to your fathers.
units.Ezekiel 20:43: There you will remember your ways and your practices by which you were being defiled; you will beat your faces over all your evils.
units.Ezekiel 20:44: You will recognize that I am the Lord when I deal thus with you so that My name may not be profaned according to your evil ways and corrupt practices, says the Lord.’”
units.Ezekiel 21:1: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 21:2: “Son of man, set your face firmly toward Thaiman, look toward Darom, and prophesy against the leading forest, Nageb,
units.Ezekiel 21:3: and say to the Nageb forest, ‘Hear the Lord’s word! Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am kindling a fire within you. It will devour every green tree and every dry tree in you. The kindled flame will not be quenched, and every face from east to north will be burned by it.
units.Ezekiel 21:4: All flesh will recognize that I, the Lord, have kindled it, and it will not be quenched.’”
units.Ezekiel 21:5: I said, “By no means, Lord, Lord! They say to me, ‘Is this not a parable being spoken?’”
units.Ezekiel 21:6: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 21:7: “Therefore prophesy, son of man; set your face firmly toward Jerusalem, look toward their holy places, and prophesy against Israel’s land,
units.Ezekiel 21:8: and say to Israel’s land, ‘Behold, I am against you. I will draw My dagger from its sheath and destroy from you the unjust and the lawless.
units.Ezekiel 21:9: Because I will destroy from you the unjust and the lawless, so My dagger will come out of its sheath against all flesh from east to north.
units.Ezekiel 21:10: All flesh will recognize that I, the Lord, have drawn My dagger from its sheath, and it will not return again.’
units.Ezekiel 21:11: And you, son of man, groan deeply with your loins broken; groan in pains before their eyes.
units.Ezekiel 21:12: If they say to you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ say, ‘Because of the message, for it is coming. Every heart will be shattered, all hands will be paralyzed, all flesh and every spirit will expire, and all thighs will be defiled with moisture. Behold, it is coming and will happen, says the Lord, the Lord.’”
units.Ezekiel 21:21: Pass through! Be sharpened on the right and on the left, wherever your face may be roused.
units.Ezekiel 21:22: I too will strike My hand against My hand and release My wrath. I, the Lord, have spoken.’”
units.Ezekiel 21:23: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 21:24: “And you, son of man, arrange two roads for Babylon’s king’s sword to enter. Both will come out from one country, and a hand at the beginning of a city road; at the beginning
units.Ezekiel 21:25: of a road you will arrange for the sword to enter against Rabbath of the sons of Ammon, against Judea, and against Jerusalem in her midst.
units.Ezekiel 21:26: For Babylon’s king will stand upon the ancient road, at the beginning of the two roads, to divine a divination, toss a rod, question the carved images and inspect a liver at his right.
units.Ezekiel 21:27: The oracle came against Jerusalem: to set a siege stake, open the mouth in a shout, raise the voice with a cry, set a siege stake against her gates, cast up a mound and build missile stations.
units.Ezekiel 22:1: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
units.Ezekiel 22:2: “And you, son of man, will you judge the city of bloodshed? Display all her lawless deeds to her,
units.Ezekiel 22:3: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O city shedding blood within her so that her time may come, making reflections against herself to defile herself!
units.Ezekiel 22:4: Through their blood that you shed you have transgressed, and through your reflections that you made you were being defiled. You brought your days near and brought the season of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the countries
units.Ezekiel 22:5: near you and far away from you. They will mock you: “Unclean, the famous one, abundant in lawless deeds!”
units.Ezekiel 22:7: They reviled father and mother in you and dealt unjustly with the sojourner in you. They oppressed the orphan and widow in you.
units.Ezekiel 22:8: They despised My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths in you.
units.Ezekiel 22:9: Robbers are in you in order to shed blood in you. They ate upon the mountains in you; they committed unholy acts within you.

source_units.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, tell a story and speak a parable to the house of Israel,
and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: The great eagle, with great wings and a broad span, full of talons, which has authority to enter Lebanon, took the cedar’s choice parts;
he nipped off the tips of its tender growth, carried them to the land of Canaan, and set them in a fortified city.
He took some of the land’s seed and put it in the plain, a plant beside abundant water; he appointed it to be watched over.
It sprouted and became a weak vine, small in size so that it might appear. Its branches were upon it and its roots beneath it. It became a vine, produced offshoots and extended its climbing growth.

There was another great eagle, with great wings and many talons. Behold, this vine was intertwined toward him, its roots toward him; it sent its branches to him to water it together with the clod of its planting.
It grows fat in a good plain beside abundant water, to produce shoots, bear fruit and become a great vine.

Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Will it prosper? Will not the roots of its tender growth and its fruit rot, and all its early shoots dry up? No great arm or numerous people will be needed to pull it from its roots.
Behold, it grows fat—surely it will not prosper? Will it not dry up completely as soon as the scorching wind touches it? It will dry up together with the clod of its growth.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

“Son of man, say now to the embittering house, ‘Do you not understand what these things were?’ Say, ‘When Babylon’s king comes against Jerusalem, he will take her king and her rulers and bring them to himself in Babylon.
He will take one of the royal seed, make a covenant with him, and bring him under a curse-oath. He will take the land’s leaders,
so that it may become a weak kingdom, not exalt itself at all, and keep his covenant and establish it.

He will revolt from him, sending his messengers to Egypt to give him horses and many people. Will he prosper? Will the one doing contrary things be rescued? Will one transgressing a covenant be saved?
As I live, says the Lord, surely in the place of the king who made him king—he who dishonored My curse-oath and transgressed My covenant—with him in the midst of Babylon he will die.
Pharaoh will not wage war against him with great power or a numerous crowd, amid siegeworks and the building of missile stations to remove lives.
He dishonored a sworn oath by transgressing a covenant; behold, he has given his hand and did all these things to him. Surely he will not be saved?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: As I live, surely My covenant that he transgressed and My sworn oath that he dishonored—I will bring them upon his head.
I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in his enclosure.
In all his battle array they will fall by the sword, and I will scatter the survivors to every wind. You will recognize that I, the Lord, have spoken.’
For thus says the Lord: I Myself will take from the cedar’s choice parts, nip off from the top of their heart, and I Myself will plant it upon a high mountain. I will suspend it

upon Israel’s lofty mountain and plant it. It will produce a shoot, bear fruit and become a great cedar. Every beast will rest beneath it, every bird will rest under its shade, and its branches will be restored.
All the plain’s trees will know that I am the Lord who lowers a high tree, raises a low tree, dries a green tree and makes a dry tree flourish. I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, what is this proverb you have among Israel’s sons, saying, ‘The fathers ate unripe grapes, and the children’s teeth were set on edge’?
As I live, says the Lord, this proverb will certainly no longer be spoken in Israel.
For all souls are Mine. As the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son—they are Mine. The soul that sins will die.
The person who is righteous, practicing judgment and righteousness,

will not eat upon the mountains, certainly will not raise his eyes to the reflections of the house of Israel, certainly will not defile his neighbor’s wife, and will not approach a woman in her menstrual separation;
he certainly will not oppress anyone, will return a debtor’s pledge, takes no plunder, will give his bread to the hungry, and will clothe the naked;
he will not give his silver at interest or take increase, will turn his hand from injustice, and will render a righteous judgment between a man and his neighbor;
he has walked in My commands and kept My ordinances to carry them out. This one is righteous; he will surely live, says the Lord.
But if he fathers a pestilent son who sheds blood and commits sins,
he did not walk in the way of his righteous father, but even ate upon the mountains and defiled his neighbor’s wife,
oppressed the poor and needy, seized plunder, did not return a pledge, set his eyes upon idols, and has committed lawlessness,
gave at interest and took increase—this one certainly will not live. He committed all this lawlessness; he will surely be put to death, and his blood will be upon him.
But if he fathers a son who sees all the sins his father committed, becomes afraid, and does not act according to them,
he has not eaten upon the mountains, not set his eyes upon the reflections of the house of Israel, and not defiled his neighbor’s wife,
has not oppressed anyone, not taken a pledge, and not seized plunder; he gave his bread to the hungry and clothed the naked,
and turned his hand from injustice, did not take interest or increase, practiced righteousness and walked in My commands. He will not die in his father’s injustices; he will surely live.
But if his father practiced affliction and seized plunder, he did contrary things in the midst of My people and will die in his injustice.
You will say, ‘Why did the son not receive his father’s injustice?’ Because the son practiced righteousness and mercy, preserved all My ordinances and carried them out; he will surely live.

The soul that sins will die. The son will not receive his father’s injustice, nor the father his son’s injustice. The righteous person’s righteousness will be upon him, and the lawless person’s lawlessness upon him.
If the lawless person turns from all the lawlessness he committed, keeps all My commandments, and practices righteousness and mercy, he will surely live; he certainly will not die.
None of the transgressions he committed will be remembered. By the righteousness he practiced, he will live.
Do I at all desire the death of the lawless, says the Lord, rather than his turning from his evil way and living?

But when a righteous person turns from his righteousness and practices injustice according to all the lawlessness the lawless person committed, none of the righteous acts he did will be remembered. In the transgression he committed and the sins he sinned, in these he will die.
You said, ‘The Lord’s way does not run straight.’ Hear now, the whole house of Israel: Surely My way does not fail to run straight? Is it not your way that fails to run straight?
When the righteous person turns from his righteousness, commits a transgression and dies, in the transgression he committed—in it he will die.
When a lawless person turns from the lawlessness he practiced and practices judgment and righteousness, this one has preserved his life
and turned from all the impieties he committed; he will surely live, he certainly will not die.
The house of Israel says, ‘The Lord’s way does not go right.’ Surely My way does not fail to go right, house of Israel? Is it not your way that fails to go right?
I will judge you, each according to his way, house of Israel, says the Lord. Turn back and turn away from all your impieties, and they will not become a punishment of injustice for you.
Cast away from yourselves all your impieties with which you acted impiously against Me, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why are you dying, house of Israel?
For I do not desire the death of the one who dies, says the Lord.”
“And you, take up a lament over Israel’s ruler,
and say: What was your mother? A cub! She came to be among lions; among lions she multiplied her cubs.
One of her cubs sprang away; he became a lion, learned to seize prey, and ate human beings.
Nations heard against him; he was caught in their destruction, and they led him with a muzzle to Egypt’s land.
She saw that he had been driven away from her and that her support had perished; she took another of her cubs and appointed him a lion.
He moved among lions, became a lion, learned to seize prey, and ate human beings.
He fed in his boldness, desolated their cities, and destroyed the land and its fullness by the sound of his roaring.
Nations from the surrounding countries set themselves against him and spread their nets over him; he was caught in their destruction.
They put him in a muzzle and a cage. He came to Babylon’s king, and he brought him into prison, so that his voice would not be heard upon Israel’s mountains.
Your mother was like a vine, like a blossom on a pomegranate tree, planted by water; her fruit and her shoot came from abundant water.
She had a rod of strength for a tribe of leaders; it rose in her size among the trunks, and it saw her size among the multitude of her branches.
She was broken off in wrath and thrown to the ground. The scorching wind dried her choice parts; her rod of strength was punished and dried up. Fire consumed her.
Now they have planted her in the wilderness, in a waterless land,
and fire went out from a rod of her choice parts and devoured her, and there was no rod of strength in her. A tribe is for a parable of lament, and it will become a lament.”
In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, men from the elders of the house of Israel came to question the Lord and sat before me.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, speak to Israel’s elders and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Have you come to question Me? As I live, I will certainly not answer you, says the Lord.’
Shall I indeed exact retribution upon them? Son of man, solemnly testify to them about their fathers’ lawlessness,

and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: From the day I chose the house of Israel, I became known to the seed of Jacob’s house and was known to them in Egypt’s land. I supported them with My hand, saying, “I am the Lord your God.”
On that day I supported them with My hand to bring them out of Egypt’s land into the land I prepared for them, a land flowing with milk and honey; it is a honeycomb compared with all the earth.
I said to them, “Let each cast away the abominations of his eyes, and do not be defiled by Egypt’s practices. I am the Lord your God.”

They revolted from Me and would not listen to Me. They did not cast away the abominations of their eyes or abandon Egypt’s practices. I said I would pour My wrath upon them and complete My anger in them in the midst of Egypt’s land.
I acted so that My name would not be profaned at all before the nations among whom they are, among whom I was known to them before their eyes by bringing them out of Egypt’s land.
I brought them out of Egypt’s land and brought them into the wilderness,
and gave them My commands and made My ordinances known to them, which a person will carry out and by which he will live.
I gave them My sabbaths as a sign between Me and them, so that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them.

I said to the house of Israel in the wilderness, “Walk in My commands.” But they did not walk, and they rejected My ordinances, which a person will carry out and by which he will live; they greatly profaned My sabbaths. I said I would pour My wrath upon them in the wilderness to consume them utterly.
I acted so that My name would not be profaned at all before the nations from whom I brought them out before their eyes.
I too raised My hand against them in the wilderness, that I would not bring them at all into the land I gave them, a land flowing with milk and honey, a honeycomb compared with all the earth,
because they rejected My ordinances, did not walk in My commands, and were profaning My sabbaths, and they followed the reflections of their hearts.
My eye spared them from obliteration, and I did not make a complete end of them in the wilderness.
I said to their children in the wilderness, “Do not walk in your fathers’ ordinances, do not keep their judgments, do not mix yourselves with their practices, and do not be defiled.
I am the Lord your God. Walk in My commands, keep My ordinances and carry them out,
and sanctify My sabbaths; let it be a sign between Me and you, so that you may know that I am the Lord your God.”

Their children too embittered Me. They did not walk in My commands or keep My ordinances to carry them out, which a person will carry out and by which he will live; they were profaning My sabbaths. I said I would pour My wrath upon them in the wilderness and complete My anger upon them.
I acted so that My name would not be profaned at all before the nations from whom I brought them out before their eyes.
I raised My hand against them in the wilderness, to scatter them among the nations and disperse them among the countries,
because they did not carry out My ordinances, rejected My commands and were profaning My sabbaths, while their eyes followed their fathers’ reflections.
I too gave them commands that were not good, and ordinances in which they would not live.
I will defile them through their gifts, when I pass through every one who opens the womb, so that I may destroy them.
Therefore speak to the house of Israel, son of man, and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: To this extent your fathers angered Me in the transgressions they committed against Me.

I brought them into the land I raised My hand to give them. They saw every high hill and every shady tree; there they sacrificed to their gods, there they set a fragrant aroma, and there they poured their libations.
I said to them, “What is Abama, that you go in there?” They called its name Abama to this very day.’
Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord: Are you being defiled in your fathers’ lawlessness and prostituting yourselves after their abominations?

In the firstfruits of your gifts, in your separations, you are being defiled with all your reflections to this very day. Shall I answer you, house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord, I will certainly not answer you, nor will this rise upon your spirit.
It will not be as you say: “We will be like the nations and like the tribes of the earth, serving woods and stones.”
Therefore, as I live, says the Lord, with a mighty hand, a high arm and outpoured wrath I will reign over you.
I will bring you out from the peoples and receive you from the countries where you were scattered, with a mighty hand, a high arm and outpoured wrath.
I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples and contend with you there, face to face.
As I contended with your fathers in the wilderness of Egypt’s land, so I will judge you, says the Lord.
I will lead you beneath My rod and bring you in by number,
and select from you the impious and those who have revolted, for I will bring them out of their sojourning, but they will not enter Israel’s land. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

And you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord, the Lord: Each of you, remove his practices! After these things, if you are not listening to Me, you will no longer profane My holy name with your gifts and practices.

For upon My holy mountain, upon a high mountain, says the Lord, the Lord, there the whole house of Israel will serve Me to the end. There I will accept, and there I will attend to your firstfruits and the firstfruits of your separations, with all your holy things.
As a fragrant aroma I will accept you when I bring you out from the peoples and receive you from the countries where you were scattered. I will be sanctified among you before the eyes of the peoples.
You will recognize that I am the Lord when I bring you into Israel’s land, into the land for which I raised My hand to give it to your fathers.
There you will remember your ways and your practices by which you were being defiled; you will beat your faces over all your evils.
You will recognize that I am the Lord when I deal thus with you so that My name may not be profaned according to your evil ways and corrupt practices, says the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face firmly toward Thaiman, look toward Darom, and prophesy against the leading forest, Nageb,

and say to the Nageb forest, ‘Hear the Lord’s word! Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am kindling a fire within you. It will devour every green tree and every dry tree in you. The kindled flame will not be quenched, and every face from east to north will be burned by it.
All flesh will recognize that I, the Lord, have kindled it, and it will not be quenched.’”
I said, “By no means, Lord, Lord! They say to me, ‘Is this not a parable being spoken?’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Therefore prophesy, son of man; set your face firmly toward Jerusalem, look toward their holy places, and prophesy against Israel’s land,
and say to Israel’s land, ‘Behold, I am against you. I will draw My dagger from its sheath and destroy from you the unjust and the lawless.
Because I will destroy from you the unjust and the lawless, so My dagger will come out of its sheath against all flesh from east to north.
All flesh will recognize that I, the Lord, have drawn My dagger from its sheath, and it will not return again.’
And you, son of man, groan deeply with your loins broken; groan in pains before their eyes.

If they say to you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ say, ‘Because of the message, for it is coming. Every heart will be shattered, all hands will be paralyzed, all flesh and every spirit will expire, and all thighs will be defiled with moisture. Behold, it is coming and will happen, says the Lord, the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, prophesy and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Say: Sword, sword, be sharpened and enraged,
so that you may slaughter victims. Be sharpened to become gleaming. Ready for paralysis, slaughter! Disdain; thrust away every tree.
He gave it ready for his hand to grasp. The sword has been sharpened; it is ready to be put into the hand of one who pierces.
Cry aloud and wail, son of man, for it has come among My people, among all Israel’s leaders. They will sojourn upon a sword; it has come among My people. Therefore strike upon your hand.
For it has been justified. And what if even a tribe was rejected? It will not be, says the Lord, the Lord.
And you, son of man, prophesy and strike hand upon hand, and double the sword. The third sword of the wounded is the great sword of the wounded, and it will terrify them,
so that the heart is shattered and the weak multiply at every gate of theirs. They have been handed over as victims of a sword. It has been well prepared for slaughter, well prepared for gleaming.
Pass through! Be sharpened on the right and on the left, wherever your face may be roused.
I too will strike My hand against My hand and release My wrath. I, the Lord, have spoken.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“And you, son of man, arrange two roads for Babylon’s king’s sword to enter. Both will come out from one country, and a hand at the beginning of a city road; at the beginning
of a road you will arrange for the sword to enter against Rabbath of the sons of Ammon, against Judea, and against Jerusalem in her midst.
For Babylon’s king will stand upon the ancient road, at the beginning of the two roads, to divine a divination, toss a rod, question the carved images and inspect a liver at his right.
The oracle came against Jerusalem: to set a siege stake, open the mouth in a shout, raise the voice with a cry, set a siege stake against her gates, cast up a mound and build missile stations.
He is to them like one divining a divination before them, and he himself recalls his injustices for remembrance.

Therefore thus says the Lord: Because you recalled your injustices when your impieties were revealed, so that your sins were seen in all your impieties and practices—because you recalled them, in these you will be captured.
And you, profane, lawless leader of Israel, whose day has arrived in a season of injustice—an end!—
thus says the Lord: You removed the tiara and put on the crown. This will not be such. You lowered the high and raised the low.
Injustice, injustice I will make it! Nor will this be such until the one comes to whom it belongs, and I will hand it over to him.

And you, son of man, prophesy and say, ‘Thus says the Lord concerning the sons of Ammon and their reproach.’ Say, ‘Sword, sword, drawn for victims and drawn for complete destruction, arise so that you may gleam,
in your vain vision and your divining false things, to hand you over upon the necks of the wounded lawless, whose day has arrived in a season of injustice—an end!
Turn back; do not lodge in this place where you were born. In your own land I will judge you
and pour My anger upon you. I will blow upon you with the fire of My anger and hand you into the hands of barbarian men devising destruction.
You will be food in fire; your blood will be in the midst of your land. There certainly will be no remembrance of you, for I, the Lord, have spoken.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“And you, son of man, will you judge the city of bloodshed? Display all her lawless deeds to her,
and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: O city shedding blood within her so that her time may come, making reflections against herself to defile herself!

Through their blood that you shed you have transgressed, and through your reflections that you made you were being defiled. You brought your days near and brought the season of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the countries
near you and far away from you. They will mock you: “Unclean, the famous one, abundant in lawless deeds!”
Behold, the leaders of Israel’s house mingled themselves in you, each with his relatives, in order to shed blood.
They reviled father and mother in you and dealt unjustly with the sojourner in you. They oppressed the orphan and widow in you.
They despised My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths in you.
Robbers are in you in order to shed blood in you. They ate upon the mountains in you; they committed unholy acts within you.
They uncovered a father’s shame in you, and they violated a woman sitting apart in uncleanness in you.
Each acted lawlessly with his neighbor’s wife; each defiled his daughter-in-law with impiety; each violated his sister, his father’s daughter, in you.
They took gifts in you in order to shed blood; they took interest and increase in you. You brought your evil in oppression to its full completion, but you forgot Me, says the Lord.
But if I strike My hand against My hand over what you have completed, what you did, and over your bloodshed that occurred within you,
will your heart hold out? Will your hands prevail in the days when I act within you? I, the Lord, have spoken and will act.
I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you among the countries, and your uncleanness will cease from you.
I will take possession in you before the nations’ eyes, and you will know that I am the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, behold, Israel’s house has become mixed to Me, all of them with copper, iron, tin and lead; it is mixed amid silver.
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because all of you became one mixture, therefore I am receiving you into Jerusalem.
As silver, copper, iron, tin and lead are received into a furnace to blow fire into it to melt it, so I will receive you in My anger, gather you and melt you,
and blow upon you with the fire of My anger, and you will be melted within her.
As silver is melted within a furnace, so you will be melted within her. You will recognize that I, the Lord, have poured My wrath upon you.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, say to her, ‘You are a land not wetted, nor did rain come upon you on the day of wrath.
Her leaders within her are like roaring lions seizing prey, devouring lives with power, taking payments unjustly, and your widows have multiplied within you.

Her priests set aside My law and profaned My holy things. They did not distinguish between holy and profane, nor distinguish between unclean and clean. They covered their eyes from My Sabbaths, and I was profaned among them.
Her rulers within her are like wolves seizing prey to shed blood, so that in greed they may gain more.
Her prophets, coating them, will fall, seeing vain things, divining falsehoods, saying, “Thus says the Lord,” when the Lord has not spoken,
oppressing the people of the land unjustly and seizing plunder, oppressing the poor and needy and not dealing justly with the sojourner.
I sought among them a man conducting himself rightly and standing wholly before Me at the land’s time, so that I would not utterly wipe her out, but I found none.
I poured My wrath upon her in the fire of My anger to bring an end. I brought their ways upon their own heads, says the Lord, the Lord.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother,
and they prostituted themselves in Egypt in their youth. There their breasts fell; there they were deflowered.
Their names were Oholah the elder and Oholibah her sister. They became Mine and bore sons and daughters. Their names: Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem is Oholibah.
Oholah prostituted herself away from Me and set her desire upon her lovers, the Assyrians approaching her,
clothed in blue-purple, leaders and generals; all choice young men, horsemen riding horses.
She bestowed her prostitution upon them, all choice sons of Assyrians; and with all upon whom she set her desire, in all her reflections she was defiled.
She did not abandon her prostitution from Egypt, for they lay with her in her youth; they deflowered her and poured their prostitution upon her.
Therefore I handed her into her lovers’ hands, into the hands of Assyrians’ sons, upon whom she had set her desire.
They uncovered her shame, took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a subject of talk among women, and they inflicted punishments upon her, upon the daughters.
Her sister Oholibah saw this and corrupted her desire beyond hers, and her prostitution beyond her sister’s prostitution.
She set her desire upon Assyrians’ sons, leaders and generals near her, clothed in finely bordered garments, horsemen riding horses; all choice young men.
I saw that she was defiled; one way for the two.
She added to her prostitution and saw men depicted upon the wall, images of Chaldeans drawn with a stylus,
girded with embroidered work at their waists, with dyed tiaras upon their heads, all with a threefold appearance, the likeness of Chaldeans’ sons from their native land.
She set her desire upon them at the sight of her eyes and sent messengers to them in the Chaldeans’ land.
Babylon’s sons came to her, to a bed of lodgers, and defiled her in her prostitution. She was defiled by them, and her soul withdrew from them.
She uncovered her prostitution and uncovered her shame. My soul withdrew from her, as My soul had withdrawn from her sister.
You multiplied your prostitution to recall the days of your youth, in which you prostituted yourself in Egypt,
and you set your desire upon the Chaldeans, whose flesh was like donkeys’ and whose genitals were horses’ genitals.
You revisited the lawlessness of your youth, what you did in Egypt at your lodging, where your youthful breasts were.
Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord: Behold, I am rousing your lovers against you, those from whom your soul withdrew. I will bring them against you all around:
Babylon’s sons and all the Chaldeans, Phakoud, Soue and Koue, and all Assyrians’ sons with them, choice young men, all leaders and generals, threefold men and renowned men riding horses.

All will come against you from the north: chariots and wheels with a multitude of peoples, large shields and small shields; they will set a guard against you all around. I will set judgment before them, and they will punish you by their judgments.

I will set My jealousy within you, and they will deal with you in fierce anger. They will remove your nose and ears and strike down your remaining people with the sword. They will take your sons and daughters, and fire will consume your remaining people.
They will strip you of your clothing and take the objects of your boasting.
I will turn your impieties away from you and your prostitution from Egypt’s land. You certainly will not lift your eyes toward them, and you certainly will no longer remember Egypt.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am handing you into the hands of those you hate, those from whom your soul withdrew.

They will deal with you in hatred and take all the fruit of your pain and toil. You will be naked and exposed to shame, and the shame of your prostitution and your impiety will be uncovered. Your prostitution
did these things to you when you prostituted yourself after nations and were defiled in their reflections.
You walked in your sister’s way; I will put her cup into your hands.
Thus says the Lord: You will drink your sister’s cup, deep and wide, abounding to bring about
drunkenness; you will be filled with collapse. And the cup of annihilation, your sister Samaria’s cup—
you will drink it. I will turn away her festivals and her new moons, for I have spoken, says the Lord.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Because you forgot Me and cast Me behind your body, you too must take your impiety and your prostitution.”
The Lord said to me, “Son of man, will you not judge Oholah and Oholibah? Declare their lawless deeds to them,
for they committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their reflections, and made their children whom they bore to Me pass through fire offerings for them.
They even did these things to Me: they defiled My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths.
When they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered My holy places to profane them. Indeed, they acted this way within My house.
Indeed, for the men coming from far away, to whom they sent messengers—as soon as they arrived, you immediately bathed, painted your eyes with antimony and adorned yourself with ornaments,
and sat upon a spread couch with an adorned table before it. My incense and My oil—they delighted in them.
They struck up a harmonious sound. With men arriving from the mass of people out of the wilderness, they gave bracelets for their hands and a crown of boasting upon their heads.
I said, ‘Do they not commit adultery in these things? A prostitute’s deeds—and she herself prostituted herself!’
They entered her as they enter a prostitute; so they entered Oholah and Oholibah to commit lawlessness.
Righteous men will punish them with the punishment of an adulteress and the punishment of bloodshed, for they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands.

from choice animals taken. Burn the bones beneath them. It boiled, it boiled, and her bones have been cooked within her.
Therefore thus says the Lord: O city of bloodshed! A cauldron with rust in it, whose rust has not come out of her! He brought it out limb by limb; no lot fell upon her.
For her blood is within her. I have set it upon smooth rock; I have not poured it upon the earth to cover it with earth.
To make wrath rise for vengeance to be exacted, I have set her blood upon smooth rock so that it will not be covered.

and it stands upon the coals, so that its copper is scorched and heated and melts amid its uncleanness, and its rust ceases,

I, the Lord, have spoken, and it will come, and I will act. I will not draw back, nor will I show mercy. According to your ways and your reflections I will judge you, says the Lord. Therefore I will judge you according to your bloodshed, and according to your reflections I will judge you, the unclean one, the famous one, abundant in provoking.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, behold, I am taking the desires of your eyes from you in battle array. You certainly will not beat your breast, nor be wept over.

It is a groaning of blood, of loins, of mourning. Your hair will not be plaited upon you, nor will your footwear be on your feet. You certainly will not be comforted by their lips or eat the bread of men.
I spoke to the people in the morning as He commanded me, and my wife died in the evening. In the morning I did as I was ordered.
The people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things are that you are doing?”
I said to them, “The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

‘Say to Israel’s house, Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am profaning My holy things, the boast of your strength, the desires of your eyes, those for whom your souls care. Your sons and daughters whom you left behind will fall by the sword.
You will do as I have done: you will not be comforted from their mouth or eat the bread of men,
with your hair upon your heads and your footwear on your feet. You certainly will neither beat your breasts nor weep; you will waste away in your injustices and each will comfort his brother.
Ezekiel will be a portent for you; according to everything he has done, you will do when these things come. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

And you, son of man, will it not be on the day when I take their strength from them, the exaltation of their boasting, the desires of their eyes, the exaltation of their soul, their sons and daughters—
on that day the survivor will come to you to announce it into your ears?
On that day your mouth will be opened toward the survivor; you will speak and certainly will no longer be struck mute. You will be a portent for them, and they will recognize that I am the Lord.’”
